subject: Secure deployment acceptance & evidence exchange for Meridian Health (private/VPC)
messages:
From: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@meridianhealth.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@meridianhealth.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@meridianhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Meridian - Private/VPC acceptance evidence & clarifications

Thanks Jordan & Vanessa — following our internal readiness review, we need a short package of artifacts to complete our security acceptance checklist before we sign off on the private/VPC deployment. High level asks:

- Network diagram showing isolated subnets, egress controls, and where operator machines connect (diagram PDF preferred)
- KMS/HSM integration details and whether customer-managed keys are supported (FIPS/HSM model numbers helpful)
- Operator access model (least-privilege IAM roles, break-glass procedures, MFA)
- Patch/update process for air-gapped/offline instances and estimated maintenance windows
- Any SOC2 / ISO artifacts you can share or attestations relevant to isolated deployments

We've attached our internal acceptance checklist (Meridian_Acceptance_v1.xlsx) for your reference. Can you confirm whether you can provide a short evidence pack and a proposed 2-week maintenance blackout window for initial rollout?

Appreciate a reply by end of day Wednesday so our program team can finalize the timetable.

Regards,
Alex Monroe
Director, Infrastructure Security
Meridian Health

(Attachment: Meridian_Acceptance_v1.xlsx)

From: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Nov 2028 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Meridian - Private/VPC acceptance evidence & clarifications

Thanks Alex — we can assemble a compact evidence pack targeted at the items you listed. Quick plan:

1) I will send a short evidence checklist (PDF) that maps Redwood artifacts to your acceptance items.
2) Vanessa will supply the KMS/HSM architecture PDF and network diagram stub.
3) Ben will confirm patch cadence and suggested maintenance blackout windows.
4) Irene (ops) will provide an operator runbook excerpt and break-glass procedures.

We typically support customer-managed KMS via an HSM-backed key provider (we will include model numbers and FIPS status). For air-gapped installs the patch flow is: offline image signing, staged rollout, operator-led verification; we'll include the step-by-step in the runbook extract.

Draft evidence (attached) — "20281119-meridian-evidence-checklist.pdf" — should get you most of what's needed; Vanessa and Irene are looping in additional artifacts. If you prefer a quick call, I'm available Wed 11:00–12:30 PST.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: 20281119-meridian-evidence-checklist.pdf)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@meridianhealth.com>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Nov 2028 12:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Meridian - Private/VPC acceptance evidence & clarifications

Alex — adding technical detail on KMS and network layout. Summary highlights:

- KMS/HSM: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMIP-compatible HSMs or cloud KMS (BYOK). For on-prem we have validated integration with Thales Luna 7xxx and Utimaco HSMs; both FIPS 140-2 Level 3 options. We'll attach a short architecture diagram (kms-hsm-architecture.pdf) and a config checklist.

- Network: attached is a network diagram (network-diagram-v1.png) showing dedicated management subnets with a bastion jumpbox, explicit egress deny-by-default rules, and an egress gateway where copy-data/export policies are enforced. For air-gapped sites we can provide an offline bundle transfer procedure.

- Operator access: we recommend per-operator short-lived certs + MFA for the operator bastion; operator accounts are scoped to non-production namespaces until acceptance is complete. Break-glass requires two-person approval captured in audit logs.

I'll leave the runbook excerpt to Irene — we've kept our artifacts intentionally concise for procurement review.

Attachments: network-diagram-v1.png, kms-hsm-architecture.pdf

—Vanessa
VP, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@meridianhealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@meridianhealth.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@meridianhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Nov 2028 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Meridian - Private/VPC acceptance evidence & clarifications

Thanks — a few follow-ups from our compliance and procurement teams:

- Please confirm any SOC2/ISO attestations that cover the deployed control plane (even if hosted control plane remains Redwood-managed). A redacted SOC2 report or SOC2 letter would be helpful.
- For HSM claims, procurement requires FIPS certificate references and whether key material ever leaves the HSM (we expect it not to).
- Maintenance window: Meridian prefers a rolling weekday maintenance window 23:00–03:00 PST; is a 2-hour window nightly during rollout feasible? If not, propose an alternative.
- Contracts: Contracts team will need a DocuSign link with the SOW addendum referencing the private deployment specifics. Can you route?

We'll hold the signing until we get the evidence pack and a confirmation on maintenance windows.

Best,
Priya Singh
Program Manager, Meridian Health
(Contracts: contracts@meridianhealth.com)

From: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@meridianhealth.com>, Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Nov 2028 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Meridian - Private/VPC acceptance evidence & clarifications

Hi all — attaching an operator runbook extract with concrete steps for acceptance verification and the offline patch process. Key excerpts:

- Operator onboarding: identity verification, MFA enrollment, RBAC role binding template, and audit logging steps.
- Break-glass flow: emergency key escrow requires two on-call approvers; actions are logged to local audit store; timestamps and approvers exported to customer telemetry via signed artifact.
- Offline patch process (air-gapped): vendor-signed image creation -> checksum signing using customer HSM -> transfer via encrypted media to staging -> operator-led validation -> staged rollout with health checks every 15 minutes for first two hours. Estimated per-node maintenance 30–45 minutes; we recommend nightly 23:00–02:00 PST for the initial rollout to allow retries.

Attachment: operator-runbook-extract.txt

If Meridian's procurement needs a signed attestation covering the runbook practices, we can prepare a short attestation letter on Redwood letterhead.

—Irene Choi
Director, Field Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Monroe <alex.monroe@meridianhealth.com>

Team — this is very helpful, thanks. A couple of final items before we route to contracts for sign-off:

- Please provide the redacted SOC2 attestation or SOC2 letter and confirm which Redwood controls apply to the private deployment operational model (control plane vs. data plane split).
- Confirm the HSM model numbers and that key material never leaves the HSM in both BYOK and Redwood-managed KMS modes.
- Contracts: please send the DocuSign addendum (we expect a simple SOW attachment referencing the agreed maintenance window and HSM requirements).

If you can get the SOC2 letter and the DocuSign link by COB Monday, Meridian will proceed to final legal review next week. We appreciate the clarity and the runbook excerpt — that helped unblock compliance.

Alex Monroe
Director, Infrastructure Security
Meridian Health
(Attachment: Meridian_Internal_NextSteps.docx)
